arxiv-2102-07073.title: Costly Features Classification using Monte Carlo Tree Search
arxiv-2102-07073.creator: Ziheng Chen ⋆ , Jin Huang ⋆ , Hongshik Ahn ⋆ , and Xin Ning †
arxiv-2102-07073.description: Abstract In many real-world tasks, acquiring features requires a certain cost, which gives rise to the costly features classification problem. In this study, We formulate the problem in the reinforcement learning framework and sequentially select the subset of features to make a balance between the classification error and the feature cost.

arxiv-2201-07301.title: Measurement of the inclusive and differential \ttbar ​ \PGg \ttbar\PGg cross sections in the dilepton channel and effective field theory interpretation in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-2201-07301.description: Abstract The production cross section of a top quark pair in association with a photon is measured in proton-proton collisions in the decay channel with two oppositely charged leptons ( \Pepm ​ \PGmmp \Pepm\PGmmp , \Pep ​ \Pem \Pep\Pem , or \PGmp ​ \PGmm \PGmp\PGmm ).

arxiv-2212-10947.title: Parallel Context Windows for Large Language Models
arxiv-2212-10947.creator: Nir Ratner Yoav Levine Yonatan Belinkov Ori Ram Inbal Magar Omri Abend
arxiv-2212-10947.description: Abstract When applied to processing long text, Large Language Models (LLMs) are limited by their context window. Existing efforts to address this limitation involve training specialized architectures, and cannot be easily applied to off-the-shelf LLMs. We present Parallel Context Windows (PCW), a method that alleviates the context window restriction for any off-the-shelf LLM without further training .

arxiv-2310-06882.title: Understanding the Formation of Galaxies with Warm Dark Matter
arxiv-2310-06882.creator: Bruce Hoeneisen
arxiv-2310-06882.description: Abstract The formation of galaxies with warm dark matter is approximately adiabatic. The cold dark matter limit is singular and requires relaxation. In these lecture notes we develop, step-by-step, the physics of galaxies with warm dark matter, and their formation. The theory is validated with observed spiral galaxy rotation curves. These observations constrain the properties of the dark matter particles.

arxiv-2410-19009.title: Dual Space Training for GANs: A Pathway to Efficient and Creative Generative Models
arxiv-2410-19009.creator: Beka Modrekiladze
arxiv-2410-19009.description: Abstract Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have demonstrated remarkable advancements in generative modeling; however, their training is often resource-intensive, requiring extensive computational time and hundreds of thousands of epochs. This paper proposes a novel optimization approach that transforms the training process by operating within a dual space of the initial data using invertible mappings, specifically autoencoders.

arxiv-2502-11764.title: Quasinormal modes of massive scalar fields in five-dimensional Myers-Perry black holes with two arbitrary rotation parameters
arxiv-2502-11764.creator: Zi-Yang Huang, Jia-Hui Huang
arxiv-2502-11764.description: Abstract We investigate the quasinormal modes of massive scalar fields in the background of five-dimensional Myers-Perry black holes. In particular, we explore the case for Myers-Perry black holes with two arbitrary rotation parameters. Since the Klein-Gordon equation for the scalar field is separable, we numerically compute the scalar quasinormal modes by using the radial and angular equations.

arxiv-2505-02994.title: Including Bloom Filters in Bottom-up Optimization
arxiv-2505-02994.creator: Tim Zeyl, Qi Cheng, Reza Pournaghi, Jason Lam, Weicheng Wang, Calvin Wong, Chong Chen, Per-Ake Larson
arxiv-2505-02994.description: Abstract . Bloom filters are used in query processing to perform early data reduction and improve query performance. The optimal query plan may be different when Bloom filters are used, indicating the need for Bloom filter-aware query optimization. To date, Bloom filter-aware query optimization has only been incorporated in a top-down query optimizer and limited to snowflake queries.

arxiv-2507-12074.title: Testing the influence of anisotropic CR transport and the Galactic magnetic field structure on the all-sky gamma-ray emission
arxiv-2507-12074.creator: Horst Fichtner
arxiv-2507-12074.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Horst Fichtner. The spatial diffusion of energetic particles in a magnetic field composed of a large-scale background and a small-scale turbulent component should be expected to be anisotropic. While such anisotropic diffusion has been known for quite a while in first-principle plasma physics and while it is required for an understanding of the transport of cosmic rays in the heliosphere or close to supernova remnants, only in recent years it has also become of particular interest for the modeling of Galactic cosmic ray (GCR)

arxiv-2508-13012.title: An Improved Solution to the Two Normal Means Problem via Regularization
arxiv-2508-13012.creator: Yang Liu Jonathan P. Williams
arxiv-2508-13012.description: Abstract The many-normal-means problem is a classic example that motivates the development of many important inferential procedures in the history of statistics. In this short note, we consider a further special case of the problem, which involves only two normally distributed data points with a constraint that the pair of means are not too far apart from one another.

arxiv-2509-09047.title: Multi-Qubit Golden Gates
arxiv-2509-09047.creator: Rahul Dalal, Shai Evra, Ori Parzanchevski
arxiv-2509-09047.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rahul Dalal, Shai Evra, Ori Parzanchevski. Our goal in this paper is to construct optimal topological generators for compact unitary Lie groups, extending the works of [ 81 ] , [ 70 ] on golden and super-golden gates to higher dimensions. To do so we consider a variant of the Sarnak–Xue Density Hypotheses [ 78 ] , [ 77 ] in the weight aspect for definite projective unitary groups and prove it using the endoscopic classification of automorphic representations.

pmc-10597285.title: The ‘FFAB’ project: Lessons learned from an early health intervention for male sports bettors
pmc-10597285.creator: B Biggar, G Reith, H Wardle
pmc-10597285.description: BackgroundSports betting is a growth area for the gambling industry with football fans becoming a key target of advertising. This demographic is also one at elevated risk from gambling harm. This paper reflects on the NIHR-funded Football Fans and Betting project (FFAB) - an innovative early health intervention with football fans (aged 18-55) who gamble regularly to reduce their betting.

pmc-11453351.title: 8523 An Unconventional Estrogen Receptor Conformation Induces SUMO Expression in Breast Cancer Cells
pmc-11453351.creator: Govinda R Hancock, Kristen Young, Geoffrey L Greene, Sean William Fanning
pmc-11453351.description: Disclosure: G.R. Hancock: None. K. Young: None. G.L. Greene: None. S.W. Fanning: None.Competitive allosteric regulators, selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs)/degraders (SERDs) differentially manipulate receptor structure to treat and prevent metastatic breast cancers. However, their utility is limited by the ∼40% rate of disease progression due to acquired therapy resistance.

pmc-11638682.title: Wearables and Smartphones for Tracking Modifiable Risk Factors in Metabolic Health: Protocol for a Scoping Review
pmc-11638682.creator: Victoria Brügger, Tobias Kowatsch, Mia Jovanova
pmc-11638682.description: BackgroundMetabolic diseases, such as cardiovascular diseases and diabetes, contribute significantly to global mortality and disability. Wearable devices and smartphones are increasingly used to track and manage modifiable risk factors associated with metabolic diseases. However, no established guidelines exist on how to derive meaningful signals from these devices, often hampering cross-study comparisons.

pmc-11639014.title: Knowledge and Attitude of Turkish Male Health Care Workers Regarding Human Papillomavirus and Vaccination
pmc-11639014.creator: Ahmet Doğan, Meryem Sena Toker, Hasan Tahsin Gozdas, Tayibe Bal
pmc-11639014.description: This descriptive, cross-sectional survey study aimed to evaluate the knowledge of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and vaccination, related diseases, vaccination status, and attitudes toward vaccination among Turkish male health care workers (HCWs). The study was planned between June 20 and 30, 2023.

pmc-11691782.title: VALIDATION OF A COMBINED SARCOPENIA AND NUTRITION SCREENING TOOL FOR COMMUNITY-LIVING OLDER ADULTS
pmc-11691782.creator: Susan Saffel-Shrier, Amy Covington, Jing Wang
pmc-11691782.description: Malnutrition and sarcopenia are major intersecting conditions of the frailty syndrome. Both have similar symptoms to include reduced energy and protein intake along with losses of muscle and strength. These losses can lead to decreased functionality and independence culminating in poor health outcomes.

pmc-11862481.title: Eating disorders: the increase in requests for help and the optimization of resources
pmc-11862481.creator: M Campana, M Colombi, P Milanese, A Greco, C Mucci
pmc-11862481.description: IntroductionThis work aims to provide an updated overview of the eating disorders (EDs) which are a widespread pathology nowadays. Informations related to the clinical-nosographic characteristics, an in-depth analysis about systemic-relational theories and historical evolution are provided. In addition, current informations about epidemiological data, recovery, treatment related implications, new neuroscientific theories and risk factors are shown.

pmc-12706218.title: ‘This level of racism has always been there’: clinicians’ views on supporting racially minoritised university students – a qualitative study in student support services in North East England
pmc-12706218.creator: Mma Felicia Yeebo, Taf Kunorubwe, Lucy Robinson, Sarah Thwaites
pmc-12706218.description: ObjectivesTo explore the experiences of clinicians providing pastoral and mental health services to racially and ethnically minoritised students (REMS) at UK universities, aiming to understand the challenges REMS face in accessing support and to identify ways to improve service inclusivity.DesignQualitative study using semi-structured interviews.

pmc-12752659.title: Efficient Manipulation of Magnetic Domain Wall by Dual Spin‐Orbit Torque in Synthetic Antiferromagnets
pmc-12752659.creator: Hiroto Masuda, Yuta Yamane, Takaaki Dohi, Takumi Yamazaki, Rajkumar Modak, Ken‐ichi Uchida, Jun'ichi Ieda, Mathias Kläui, Koki Takanashi, Takeshi Seki
pmc-12752659.description: Current‐induced domain‐wall motion (CIDWM) in a synthetic antiferromagnet is a key phenomenon for developing potential high‐density‐packed magnetic domain‐wall memory with fast operation. Here, CIDWM is reported in the antiferromagnetically‐coupled two Co layers through the Ir interlayer sandwiched by the two Pt layers: Pt/Co/Ir/Co/Pt.

pmc-12777290.title: Essential oil extraction from clove, characterization and application
pmc-12777290.creator: Gargi Ghoshal, Tenzin Dolker, Sakshi Gupta
pmc-12777290.description: Eugenol, a beneficial nutraceuticals majorly (80–90%) found in clove, has diverse applications due to its antimicrobial and antioxidant properties. Clove is quickly engrossed by diverse organs to metabolize in the liver. To prevent premature absorption and improved activity, water solubility, encapsulation of eugenol is the best solution. Maceration and Soxhlet were performed using ethanol, methanol and water as a solvents.

pmc-12844213.title: Theoretical Investigation of Early Cancer Biomarker Sensing Using a PMMA–Gold Hybrid Quasi-D-Shaped Photonic-Crystal-Fiber-Based Surface Plasmon Resonance Biosensor
pmc-12844213.creator: Ayushman Ramola, Amit Kumar Shakya, Nezah Balal, Arik Bergman
pmc-12844213.description: In this work, a quasi-D-shaped photonic crystal fiber (PCF)-based surface plasmon resonance (SPR) biosensor is proposed and numerically investigated using the finite element method (FEM) implemented in COMSOL Multiphysics version 6.2 for the detection of cancer cells with different refractive indices. The biosensor has a coating of plasmonic material gold (Au) and a polymer coat of polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA).

pmc-13087868.title: The effects of rebound exercise on body mass index and balance in overweight and obese adults: a meta-analysis
pmc-13087868.creator: Lin Wang, Sihong Sui
pmc-13087868.description: BackgroundRebounding involves repetitive bouncing on a trampoline, a low-impact and enjoyable exercise. The purpose of this study was to explore the effects of rebound exercise on body mass index (BMI) and balance in adults who are overweight and obese.MethodThis review searched Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, and EBSCO databases for relevant articles from January 2005 to January 2025.

pmc-13191529.title: Wogonin-Loaded PLGA Sustained-Release Nanomicelle Inhibiting EGFR Pathway for Antitumor Effects in OSCC
pmc-13191529.creator: Leina Gao, Dixin Cui, Xu Gao, Xiaoling Luan, Huali Gao
pmc-13191529.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is the most prevalent malignancy of the head and neck. Current treatment strategies, including surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, are limited by moderate efficacy and severe side effects, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic approaches. Wogonin (Wo), a natural flavonoid, has shown antiproliferative, pro-apoptotic, and antimetastatic activities in various cancer models; however, its effect on OSCC has not been investigated.

pmc-13349409.title: Perfection should not hinder progress towards occupational exposure limits for psychosocial hazard: A reply to Guseva Canu and van der Molen
pmc-13349409.creator: Roman Pauli, Jessica Lang, Andreas Müller, Yacine Taibi, Thomas Kraus, Yannick Metzler
pmc-13349409.description: ual and methodological challenges associated with transferring established approaches from the assessment of non-psychosocial (ie, chemical and physical) hazards to the psychosocial domain. We also welcome that the authors share the concerns raised in our original discussion paper (2) regarding uncertainties in existing operationalizations of psychosocial hazards.

pmc-13374355.title: Effect of parent-focused interventions for screen use on developmental outcomes in young children: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13374355.creator: Amanda Machell, Carrie Ewin, Sharon Horwood, Katherine L Downing, Kylie D Hesketh
pmc-13374355.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionParents are a key target for interventions promoting healthy screen use in young children, but no review has evaluated the effect of such parent-focused interventions on developmental outcomes in early childhood. The objective of this study was to conduct a systematic review and meta-analyses of the effects of parent-focused interventions for screen use on young children’s social-emotional, cognitive, and physical development, as well as proximal indicators of development including sleep and physical activity.

pmc-13474192.title: Electric‐Field‐Controlled Interconversion of Antiferromagnetic States in a Two‐Dimensional Antiferroelectric Halide Perovskite
pmc-13474192.creator: Wan Zhao, Xiaodong Zhou, Tao Zhu, Jie Chen, Hang Li, Jingyan Chen, Meiling Xu, Wenhong Wang
pmc-13474192.description: Electric‐field control of spin‐dependent electronic structures in antiferromagnets is highly desirable for low‐power spintronic devices, however, such control remains largely unexplored. Here, we propose a promising route based on electric‐field‐driven switching between symmetry‐distinct altermagnetic (AM) and type‐IV antiferromagnetic (AFM) states, enabling reversible interconversion between spin‐split and spin‐degenerate electronic structures.

pmc-13589061.title: Vision-threatening ocular toxoplasmosis involving the fovea diagnosed by intraocular fluid mNGS: A case report
pmc-13589061.creator: Sijian Xie, Li Wu, Ying Liu, Shangping Jiang, Yijing Yang, Qinghua Peng
pmc-13589061.description: Ocular toxoplasmosis is the most common cause of infectious posterior uveitis worldwide and may lead to irreversible visual impairment when the macula is involved. Definitive diagnosis remains challenging because clinical manifestations overlap with those of other infectious and inflammatory retinal disorders.
